info.title: Broker Portal API
info.description: This documentation serves as a guide to integrate with Vivid Seats' Broker Portal API

get.description:
This will return a list of Vivid Seats matching events. The value for eventId returned is analogous to productionId in the listings API. Every call will return up to 1000 entries. Pagination with 'page' parameter can be used to get more results. If 'eventKeyword' or 'venueKeyword' are specified, only a MAX of 1000 entries (only one page) will be returned. Otherwise ALL events will be returned thru pagination. If there is no element for the specified 'page', it will return no entries. If request is using fromDate, it must also have a toDate, otherwise error will return.
Rate limit: one request every 5 seconds.

This will return all matching events associated with your listed inventory. The value for eventId returned is analogous to productionId in the listings api.</br>Rate Limit: One request every 5 seconds

XML or JSON response.
The deleteListing method allows you to delete a listing in real-time.
Not rate limited

XML response
The getListings method will return active listings in your broker account.
Rate limit: 1 request per ticketId every 2 minutes.

post.description:
XML or JSON responses.
The updateListing method allows you to update a listing in real-time.
Only parameters you pass in to the method will be updated. The ticketId is your internal unique ID associated with the listing.
Not rate limited

This endpoint creates a new listing in the Vivid Seats Marketplace.

eventName, venue, eventDate fields are required. productionId is optional.

If the productionId is not included, the create listing request may be sent to our mapping team, and there may be a delay adding the listing to the Marketplace.
Rate limit: 50 requests per second.

put.description:
All the fields including attributes and tickets will be updated with the object passed in. This method will only work if the Content-Type header is set to application/json. An alternative version is /listings/v1/updateListing as it only requires you to supply your internal ticketID. If you want to use v2 and you only have a ticketId then you need to get the listing by ticket id first.
Rate limit: 50 requests per second.
